questions.q: What is the real difference between data residency and data sovereignty?
options: They mean exactly the same thing and are used interchangeably with no distinction
Residency applies only to video files; sovereignty applies only to text data
Sovereignty is a marketing term with no legal basis
Residency is about where data is physically stored; sovereignty is about whose laws govern it and which legal process can compel access, regardless of location
questions.explain: Residency answers 'in which physical country/region is this data stored,' while sovereignty answers 'whose laws apply, and who can be legally compelled to access it' -- a dataset can satisfy residency while still raising sovereignty concerns.

questions.q: What did the Schrems II ruling actually do?
options: It created the GDPR from scratch in 2020

It invalidated the EU-US Privacy Shield framework, because US surveillance law gave US authorities access to EU personal data in ways incompatible with EU protections, even when the data was physically stored in the EU
It banned all cloud computing within the European Union
It required every company to store data on physical tape backups only
questions.explain: Schrems II (2020, Court of Justice of the European Union) invalidated the EU-US Privacy Shield, showing that sovereignty concerns exist independently of where data is physically stored -- US legal reach over a US company mattered even for EU-stored data.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, currently enforced data-localization regime mentioned in this lesson, besides GDPR?
options: Russia's data localization law, requiring personal data of Russian citizens to be initially stored on servers within Russia
A fictional "Global Data Accord" that applies to every country equally
A rule that all data must be stored exclusively on-premises, never in any cloud
A requirement that all cloud data be stored in Antarctica for neutrality
questions.explain: Russia's data localization law and China's Cybersecurity Law/PIPL are real, enforced data-localization regimes requiring certain data to be stored or assessed before crossing borders.

questions.q: What is Microsoft's EU Data Boundary, as described in this lesson?
options: A physical fence around Microsoft's European data centers
A pricing discount for European customers only
A deprecated feature no longer offered by Microsoft
A commitment that, for in-scope Microsoft cloud services, EU customer data and its processing stay within the EU
questions.explain: The EU Data Boundary is a real Microsoft commitment keeping in-scope EU customer data and its processing within the EU, directly addressing both residency and much of the sovereignty concern.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should cross-region reporting typically work when strict residency/sovereignty requirements apply?
options: Raw personal records should be freely copied to a central region for convenience
Reporting should be disabled entirely for regulated data
Only aggregated or anonymized summaries should cross borders for central reporting, while the underlying personal records stay within their required jurisdiction
All regions should share one single global database with no regional separation
questions.explain: The practical pattern is per-region deployments with their own in-region data, where only already-aggregated, non-personal summaries are pulled upward for central reporting -- the underlying records never leave their required jurisdiction.
